title: Fix bugs in Go custom sorting functions
description: Brownfield Go dirty_cleanup: fix three intentional bugs in sorting helpers (SortByLen sorts ascending instead of descending, SortUniq doesn't deduplicate, SortDesc sorts ascending).

task_spec.prompt:
Fix three bugs in sortutils.go.

Bug 1 — SortByLen: sorts ascending (< length) instead of descending.
  Fix: change `len(out[i]) < len(out[j])` to `len(out[i]) > len(out[j])`

Bug 2 — SortUniq: doesn't remove duplicates.
  Fix: after sorting, walk the slice and keep only first occurrences:
    seen := map[int]bool{}
    uniq := out[:0]
    for _, v := range out { if !seen[v] { seen[v]=true; uniq=append(uniq,v) } }
    return uniq

Bug 3 — SortDesc: sorts ascending instead of descending.
  Fix: use sort.Sort(sort.Reverse(sort.IntSlice(out))) or sort.Slice with > comparison

All 5 tests must pass.
Run: go test ./...
required_artifacts: SortByLen returns strings ordered longest to shortest
SortUniq returns sorted slice with no duplicate values
SortDesc returns integers from largest to smallest
All edge cases (empty, single element) handled
followup_prompts: Run `go test ./...` to check the current state. Walk me through what bugs you found and fixed. If any tests are still failing, show me the errors and fix them.
Final verification: run `go test ./...` and confirm a completely clean build. Every test must pass — if any are still red, fix them now.
